title: MetaCluster: Enabling Deep Compression of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
claim: Jointly training a meta-learner organizes parameters into a low-dimensional manifold, whereas the unaided baseline leaves them as unstructured clutter.
layout: 3 panels in a row, left-to-right, t-SNE scatter plots with captions below
description: Three side-by-side t-SNE scatter plots of KAN activation weights, all drawn as dense blue points on white with axes labeled t-SNE 1 and t-SNE 2. Panel (a), the meta-learner with a 1D embedding, shows weights forming thin, winding curves that look like a maze or fingerprint, a nearly one-dimensional manifold. Panel (b), the meta-learner with a 2D embedding, shows clumpy, sheet-like structures separated by gaps. Panel (c), the plain KAN baseline, is a dense, uniform blob with no visible structure. The eye goes first to the striking curve pattern in (a), then follows the progressive loss of structure from left to right. Captions below each panel read (a) Meta-learner when d_emb=1, (b) Meta-learner when d_emb=2, (c) KAN.
caption: T-SNE visualization of KAN activation weights with and without the meta-learner $M_\theta$. (a) With a 1D embedding, the MetaKAN learns a nearly one-dimensional manifold, (b) with a 2D embedding, it learns a structured two-dimensional manifold, while (c) the baseline KAN without a meta-learner fails to organize the weights into a coherent low-dimensional structure.
abstract: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) replace scalar weights with per-edge vectors of basis coefficients, thereby increasing expressivity and accuracy while also resulting in a multiplicative increase in parameters and memory. We propose MetaCluster, a framework that makes KANs highly compressible without sacrificing accuracy. Specifically, a lightweight meta-learner, trained jointly with the KAN, maps low-dimensional embeddings to coefficient vectors, thereby shaping them to lie on a low-dimensional manifold that is amenable to clustering. We then run K-means in coefficient space and replace per-edge vectors with shared centroids. Afterwards, the meta-learner can be discarded, and a brief fine-tuning of the centroid codebook recovers any residual accuracy loss. The resulting model stores only a small codebook and per-edge indices, exploiting the vector nature of KAN parameters to amortize storage across multiple coefficients. On MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, across standard KANs and ConvKANs using multiple basis functions, MetaCluster achieves a reduction of up to $80\times$ in parameter storage, with no loss in accuracy. Similarly, on high-dimensional equation modeling tasks, MetaCluster achieves a parameter reduction of $124.1\times$, without impacting performance. Code will be released upon publication.
